findings.title: F60 reduction changes the represented value for partial base factors
findings.evidence: reduce divides num by gcd(num,60^scale), but decrements scale only for whole factors of 60 (lines 43–51).
findings.trigger: BA.EXACT dividing numerator 2 by 60 produces F60::new(2,1); gcd=2 divides numerator to 1 without changing scale.
findings.impact: The result becomes 1/60 instead of 1/30; ordinary exact arithmetic is silently corrupted.

findings.title: Division ignores the denominator scale
findings.evidence: BA.EXACT reads numerator register scale but only val2.num; val2.scale is never applied (326–337).
findings.trigger: Divide integer 1 by register containing 1/60 (obtainable by dividing 1 by 60).
findings.impact: Returns 1 rather than 60, corrupting any subsequent arithmetic on fractional operands.

findings.title: Replay digest authenticates only elapsed ticks
findings.evidence: initial hash is constant BABYLON-60-INIT and replay_hash is SHA256(self.c.to_be_bytes()); trace/state bytes never enter either hash (184–192).
findings.trigger: Run different programs or change a traced opcode while preserving final tick count.
findings.impact: Exported proof artifacts have identical replay hashes despite different programs/states; the hash cannot establish replay integrity.

findings.title: Unsupported instructions are silently accepted
findings.evidence: Opcode match fallback is _ => {}; execution then records opcode and advances PC (416–430). Assigned tools/examples/navier_stokes_hunter.b60 uses DAH, LAL, NU at lines 34,43,46, none implemented in this match.
findings.trigger: Run the supplied Navier–Stokes script or mistype an opcode.
findings.impact: Program silently skips arithmetic and branch operations; the supplied example cannot detect its advertised threshold.

findings.title: Script operands can panic the interpreter outside its halt path
findings.evidence: ALLOC unconditionally indexes tokens[1], tokens[2] and coro.r[idx]; similar unchecked reads appear in other opcodes. Register file length is 64 (455).
findings.trigger: Script contains ALLOC alone or ALLOC F60 R64.
findings.impact: Out-of-bounds panic terminates the process without critical_halt/export_artifact diagnostics.

findings.title: Unique query generator inevitably stops making progress
findings.evidence: Both query length and word indices depend exclusively on len(unique_queries); length cycles mod 6 and vocabulary indices mod len(VOCAB).
findings.impact: The candidate repeats after at most lcm(6,len(VOCAB)) distinct lengths/offsets, fewer than 1000 here. On the first duplicate set size freezes and the while loop repeats forever before inference.

findings.title: Mail migration deletes records belonging to unrelated subdomains
findings.evidence: The zone-wide records list is filtered only by MX type or TXT content v=spf1 (48–58); replacement records target only domain= babylon60.com (62–67).
findings.trigger: Zone includes MX or SPF records for a delegated mail subdomain in the returned records page.
findings.impact: Migration deletes those subdomain mail records and never restores them, disrupting unrelated mail routing and sender authorization.

findings.title: Server binds all interfaces despite announcing loopback
findings.evidence: port is :1234, log announces 127.0.0.1, then http.ListenAndServe(port,mux); handler has no authentication (46–83).
findings.trigger: Start the Go adapter on a host reachable from another machine.
findings.impact: The mock chat endpoint is exposed on all interfaces contrary to its displayed local address; remote clients can submit arbitrary request bodies.

findings.title: Monitor presents constants as live security and treasury telemetry
findings.evidence: load_telemetry_data hardcodes allocation=46.66, gate LOCKED, ring0 NOMINAL, oracle ARMED (51–54); only DB/manifests/calendar are read (57–87). UI adds biometric status, <15ns latency and total legal compliance (126–129).
findings.trigger: Run --once with missing inputs or a failed/unavailable gate.
findings.impact: Operator receives successful-looking hardware/security/compliance status and treasury allocation without observations from those systems; failures cannot change these indicators.

findings.title: Sequence validator accepts an empty normalized sequence
findings.evidence: Nonempty input is checked before upper().strip(); no emptiness check follows. Empty invalid_chars passes, seq_len=0 returns is_valid=True (87–116).
findings.trigger: Call validate_sequence with a nonempty whitespace-only sequence string.
findings.impact: Invalid empty biological input receives a valid result and the digest of empty bytes.

findings.title: Byte-sized fields are emitted as eight-byte stores
findings.evidence: Layout assigns Bool size/alignment (1,1) at 85, but Store/VolatileStore always emit mov qword [rax],rcx at 193–198; Load also uses qword.
findings.trigger: Use the public layout/backend path for a struct containing two Bool fields; its allocation is two bytes.
findings.impact: Generated assembly writes eight bytes for each Bool field, overwriting neighbors and allocated bounds. Existing Sensor example hides this by putting Bool in tail padding.

findings.title: Comment fallback directs audit output without acquiring comments
findings.evidence: On extraction failure, Phase 3b directs generation of SOCINT audit by projecting five vectors from predictable audience sociology (201–203).
findings.trigger: A comments audit cannot retrieve comments within 10 seconds or encounters anti-bot/error responses.
findings.impact: The prescribed fallback substitutes imagined audience reactions for unavailable observations; no explicit labeling requirement separates projections from an actual comments audit.

hypotheses.observation: MODEL_WEIGHT_TAMPERING is recognized by classifier but falls into BENIGN/default risk branch at 112–114.
hypotheses.uncertainty: No consumer traced to establish whether this advisory label controls an actual quarantine or loading boundary; no authorization bypass claim made.
